what: Eight rules of the frame, each on one short passage, opened by the reader itself. For a year these were drawings: a page that imitated the reader's card with typed Hebrew inside it, which demonstrates a drawing. Each of these is a real zone, built by the builder every served book goes through and opened by the same reader with the same card, and branded an instrument so that no gate can mistake it for a work.
the_law_every_card_obeys: The C0 never moves. Whatever a reader selects, the ink stands exactly as the source wrote it. Selection governs what is defined, never what is displayed.

the_tiers.CARRIED_FROM_A_NAMED_SOURCE: the ink of the passage was carried from a source this project holds, named and hashed here; the source's own credit rides on the page
the_tiers.CARRIED_WITH_THE_MARK_TYPED: the words of the passage were carried from a source this project holds, and the mark itself was typed because no source we hold writes it there; the typed positions are named in the record and drawn as typed on the page
the_tiers.TYPED_BECAUSE_NO_SOURCE_WE_HOLD_CARRIES_: no source this project holds carries the mark at all, so the ink was typed; the entry names where the wire goes, meaning the field in the corpus lane's coming reissue that will carry the real thing, so that the day it lands this passage is replaced by the book rather than repaired

the_fence: Every rule below is one of three things and says which on its face: carried whole, with its source named and hashed; carried with one mark typed into it because no source we hold writes that mark there, with the typed positions named in the record and drawn as typed on the word; or typed outright, with the reason and the wire named. No demonstration is a work: each is branded an instrument in its own file, none is listed on the door among the books, none is built by the fleet, and none is served as a work anywhere.

rules.the_c0_law: One occurrence, one C0. The complex is the word; the breakdown happens a layer down.
rules.plainly: Where the reading differed from the letters the scribes had received, they changed nothing: the written form was kept and the read form recorded beside it. The site is one word of the book, counted once, and its ink carries both forms in the source's own order.
rules.probe_notes:
SOURCE: R2 object moses-ledgers/kq-reseal-v1/streams/tanakh-nahum-kq-resealed-v1.tokens.csv.gz (sha256 0fdc43845e2e32b5bc18fb02001b1746436dab0ba26d92ed3cf5d2ee39325937), receipt tanakh-nahum-kq-resealed-v1.json (sha256 cdcfd86d3c05503b240eb930bc3dd8f46fc44bb51c36162ed1520ca33ece2793). Downloaded to /tmp/kqprobe/, nothing written into the repo. Nahum is the SMALLEST work under moses-ledgers/kq-reseal-v1/streams/ (5831 B gz, 524 token rows). RECEIPT CHECK — the normalized hash REPRODUCES, the surface hash DOES NOT. Recomputing sha256 over the surface column joined with \n plus a trailing \n gives 1e9dbba8505bf7e6581179d45fd5baad1798f69c6a15ee060763f0671ce17cc1, but the receipt's surface_token_stream_sha256 is b7f20263954d777a7059269e823ed9bade2fa267afdf01a1fb52549a44b9e8e6. The same recipe over the normalized_key column DOES match normalized_token_stream_sha256 (ea53d538153e416057c9c508ccc5563146397680854c98460456e33fa26a0879) exactly, so the join recipe itself is right and the surface digest is the odd one out. I also tried: no trailing newline, CRLF, CSV-escaped fields, header line included, raw gz bytes, raw decompressed text, NFC and NFD normalization, a space join, and the 525-row pre-merge shape with the kq row split back into (ketiv) and [qere] — none reproduce the receipt's surface hash. This is SYSTEMIC, not a Nahum quirk: I spot-checked tanakh-joel and tanakh-amos from the same prefix and both show the same pattern (normalized matches, surface does not). The builder must NOT treat surface_token_stream_sha256 in kq-reseal-v1 receipts as a verifiable seal until the lane says how it was computed; the normalized hash is trustworthy today. ROWS: the stream carries no c0 column and no unit map, so the c0 values here are the 0-based row offsets I took from the token stream (body rows 156..177 inclusive, header excluded), and unit_id is a name of my own choosing. They are contiguous and ascending but they are NOT July-body c0 ids; the builder must renumber against whatever c0 spine it serves. KQ SITE: 0-based row index 7 in rows (stream body offset 163) is the one-row ketiv-qere site — the only one in this run, and the only merged site in the whole work (receipt kq_sites_merged=1, rows_before=525, rows_after=524). Its hebrew field is the one-row form "(ketiv) [qere]". ketiv (inside parentheses): \u05dc\u05e2\u05d1\u05d5\u05e8 qere (inside brackets): \u05dc\u05b7\u05e2\u05b2\u05d1\u05c7\u05e8\u05be VOCALIZATION SITS ON THE QERE, as expected: the ketiv is 5 bare consonants with 0 marks from the Hebrew points/accents range U+0591-U+05C7; the qere carries 4 marks from that same range: patah U+05B7, hataf patah U+05B2, qamats qatan U+05C7, and a trailing maqaf U+05BE. One C0 for the site, both forms in the ink, as the source wrote them. The normalized_key for that row is the two branch keys joined by | ("לעבור|לעברבך"), per the receipt's key_law; I did not carry keys into rows, but the builder will need them. MARKUP: rejected the region around body offsets 146-147, which carry literal HTML (" {פ}
") — Sefaria MAM paragraph markers leaked into the surface column as two token rows. My run starts at 156, clear of them. These are the ONLY two markup-bearing rows in Nahum, but the builder should expect them in every work in this lane. OTHER BRACKET ROWS: body offsets 214 ("[bahalikhatam]") and 344 ("[vekhashlu]") are qere-only rows — square brackets, no parenthesized ketiv, single-branch key. They are NOT the one-row merged form and the receipt does not count them as merged sites; a frame rule keyed on "(" + "[" will skip them, which is probably right, but the builder should decide deliberately what those bracket-only rows mean.

rules.the_c0_law: Two words, two C0s, two cards. Nothing is grouped over them: the count follows the word, not the typography.
rules.plainly: A maqaf joins words into one breath and one accent. Each word it joins is its own word of the book with its own card, and the joiner rides as ink on the word before it, which is the word that gave up its accent.
rules.press: either word of a joined pair

rules.probe_notes: the corpus lane's split reseal, countersigned by the website lane 2026-09-03: the successor ink rejoins byte-equal to the 1,132 predecessor rows and both hashes reproduce. Rows 3,4,5 are the three words of one maqaf compound; rows 8,9 are a two-word compound.

rules.the_c0_law: One C0 for the abbreviated form, always on. The words it stands for get no C0 at all.
rules.plainly: An abbreviation is one token standing for several words. All of them are read, but their letters are not in the ink, so the token is the word of the book and the words it stands for are a grouping of their own. The mark between the letters is part of the key, whichever character the source wrote it with.
rules.probe_notes:
18 contiguous C0 rows from one unit (maor-vashemesh-bo-bo-15, unit_word_index 42..59), ascending, no gap. hebrew copied verbatim from the shard's `hebrew` column. No HTML markup, no maqaf, no geresh/apostrophe in the run - the only abbreviation mark present is the ASCII double quote, so the demonstration is about that mark alone.
FOUR rows carry an abbreviation mark, every one of them an ASCII U+0022 between two Hebrew letters (this work writes no U+05F4 at all in this passage):
  row 0  (c0 3830386)  mark U+0022  exactK = 'and-afterwards' abbreviation, 5 chars, gershayim at index 3 - exactK output U+05D5 U+05D0 U+05D7 U+05F4 U+05DB
  row 2  (c0 3830388)  mark U+0022  exactK = the Tetragrammaton abbreviation, U+05D4 U+05D5 U+05D9 U+05F4 U+05D4
  row 11 (c0 3830397)  mark U+0022  exactK = ha-kadosh-barukh-hu, U+05D4 U+05E7 U+05D1 U+05F4 U+05D4
  row 17 (c0 3830403)  mark U+0022  exactK = 'by means of', U+05E2 U+05F4 U+05D9
exactK was computed by importing exactK from tools/k-normalization-v2.mjs (K_RULE_ID exact-k-rule-v2-ascii-abbreviation-marks-and-boundary-maqaf). In every case it maps the ASCII U+0022 to U+05F4 and keeps it in the key; one C0 per abbreviated form, and the words it stands for get no C0 - the run is 18 C0s for 18 written words.
GLOSS MAP STATE, and this is the thing the builder must know: NONE of the four exactK keys is present in the served maor-vashemesh.bin gloss map. That zone holds 24,645 gloss keys, of which only 24 carry any abbreviation mark and all 24 use U+05F3 geresh; it holds ZERO U+05F4 gershayim keys. So under exactK v2 all four cards would carry NO reading from the zone as it stands today.
But the readings exist on the shelf. All 3,441 served zones were scanned: 179 of them do hold gershayim gloss keys, 242 distinct ones in total, and all four of these exactK keys are among them - the and-afterwards form in 37 zones ('and afterwards.'), the Tetragrammaton form in 8 zones ('Kabbalistic term for the Tetragrammaton'), ha-kadosh-barukh-hu in 53 zones ('abbreviation of ha-kadosh barukh hu'), and the by-means-of form in 44 zones (glossed as the compound preposition). A rebuild of this zone under key rule v2 would attach a correct reading to three of the four immediately, and to all four if the and-afterwards entry is pulled in.
WHAT IS SERVED TODAY IS WRONG, and this passage shows it plainly. Under the v1 key the ASCII quote was dropped and the letters ran together, so maor-vashemesh.bin currently glosses row 11 (ha-kadosh-barukh-hu) as 'the/ tent', row 17 ('by means of') as 'Ai' the place name, and row 2 (the Tetragrammaton) as 'beacon'. Three readings for forms no source wrote. Row 0's letters-run-together key is not in the map at all, so that card is simply blank. Use this run as the before/after: the same four cards, wrong or blank now, correct after the v2 rebuild.
The body's own normalized_key column is v1-shaped too (it drops the quote), so the shard's normalized_key must not be used as the card key; cut the key from the `hebrew` column with exactK.
Passage reads as continuous prose: the Holy One first told Moses the name Ehyeh and afterwards the name YHVH; the whole Torah is His names, and the worlds were created through the Torah, that is, by means of the permutations of the holy names.

rules.the_c0_law: One C0, off by default, keyless. It marks structure, not a word.
rules.plainly: A closed section mark is the scribes' bookkeeping: it says a section ends here and the next begins on the same line. It is not a word of the book and it opens no reading, so it is off until a reader turns the marks on.
rules.probe_notes: SETUMAH (frame rule 4), closed section. This unit is Exodus 20:13 in the Hebrew verse division - the block of short commandments - so the scribal setumah marks fall BETWEEN the commandments, mid-unit, not merely trailing the verse. Four of them: row 2 (c0 69800926) = "\u0028\u05e1\u0029" = samekh U+05E1 in parentheses, row 5 (c0 69800929) = "\u0028\u05e1\u0029" = samekh U+05E1 in parentheses, row 8 (c0 69800932) = "\u0028\u05e1\u0029" = samekh U+05E1 in parentheses, row 13 (c0 69800937) = "\u0028\u05e1\u0029" = samekh U+05E1 in parentheses. Each mark is its own C0 row with normalized_key 'norm:ס'; each is OFF by default and keyless. The surface is a lone samekh wrapped in ASCII parentheses U+0028/U+0029 - no braces in this unit. CLEANLINESS: all 14 rows verified free of HTML tags, class= attributes and HTML entities (no <b>, <small>, </...>, no  ). This unit was chosen over the otherwise-attractive exodus-20-14 (which carries BOTH a setumah and a petuchah in one run) because three of exodus-20-14's rows carry literal   entities - its rows 4, 6 and 15 (word indexes 4, 6, 15) each end or begin with literal   - so it is rejected under the markup rule. No single strictly-clean unit in tanakh/genesis or tanakh/exodus carries both letters, hence two files: this one and marks-petuchah.json.

rules.the_c0_law: One C0, off by default, keyless. Its own kind, beside the closed section.
rules.plainly: An open section mark says a section ends here and the next begins on a new line. Like the closed section it is the scribes' bookkeeping rather than a word of the book, and it is off until a reader turns the marks on.
rules.probe_notes: PETUCHAH (frame rule 5), open section. Row 13 (0-based; c0 69840793) carries the mark, surface "\u0028\u05e4\u0029" = a lone pe U+05E4 wrapped in ASCII parentheses U+0028/U+0029. This is Genesis 35:22, one of the rare places where the petuchah stands INSIDE the verse rather than at its end - the mark sits after row 12 and before row 14, so the passage demonstrates the mark genuinely standing between two stretches of text with 13 rows of verse before it and 4 after. The mark is its own C0 row with normalized_key 'norm:פ'; OFF by default and keyless. CLEANLINESS: all 18 rows verified free of HTML tags, class= attributes and HTML entities. See marks-setumah.json for the samekh; no strictly-clean unit in genesis or exodus holds both letters.

rules.letter: C0 · one per word, every one carded
rules.the_c0_law: Every word inside gets its own C0 and its own card. The brackets are pressable and are never toggleable.
rules.plainly: Two inverted letters stand around a short passage, and the tradition reads them as a statement about the passage itself rather than as bookkeeping. So the words inside are ordinary words with ordinary cards, the brackets can be pressed to say what they are, and no toggle may hide them: they speak about the text.
rules.press: a bracket, then a word inside
rules.typed_rows_why: the two inverted nunim are absent from every source this project holds: the probe byte-scanned all 4,646 shards of the verified body and every reseal stream and found no U+05C6. The words between them are the body's own ink; the brackets are typed so the rule can be shown at all
rules.probe_notes: NO row carries the phenomenon -- that is the finding. The inverted nun (U+05C6) does not appear in this passage in the July body; found=false. The run is 20 contiguous C0s, 70171092-70171111, ascending, ordinals 1-20. It spans the two verse units the brackets enclose: rows 0-11 (ordinals 1-12, c0 70171092-70171103) are unit numbers-10-35; rows 12-19 (ordinals 13-20, c0 70171104-70171111) are unit numbers-10-36. If the builder needs a strictly single-unit run, take rows 0-11 (numbers-10-35) alone. Where the marks WOULD go under frame rule 6: an opening nun hafukha immediately BEFORE row 0 (c0 70171092), and a closing one immediately AFTER row 19 (c0 70171111). Neither exists as a C0 in the body, so under rule 6 the brackets would have to be synthesised at render time as pressable, non-toggleable chrome; they have no C0 of their own to press. Row 19 (ordinal 20, c0 70171111) is the single letter PE (U+05E4) -- a petucha section marker that the body does carry as its own C0 inside unit numbers-10-36. The verse's last real word is row 18 (c0 70171110). Likewise the preceding verse 10:34 ends with a lone SAMEKH C0 at 70171091, just outside this run. So the body already models paragraph marks as their own C0 rows, but did not model the nun hafukha the same way. The rows are byte-for-byte verbatim from the shard's hebrew column, cantillation and sof-pasuq intact; none contains HTML markup. FOR THE RECORD, the only place U+05C6 survives in the body is Psalms 107 (work tanakh/psalms, units psalms-107-23/24/25/26/27/28/40, c0 70200260, 70200267, 70200273, 70200279, 70200286, 70200291, 70200361) and there it arrives as a broken HTML fragment glued to the first word of each verse, not as a clean standalone mark -- evidence that the mark was stripped by an HTML-unwrapping step upstream rather than never having been in the source edition.

rules.the_c0_law: Included, with its own C0, behind the toggle the section marks share.
rules.plainly: The scribes counted, and wrote their counting down: the middle of a book by verses or by words, and the tallies at its end. Those notes are text about the book rather than the book, so they are carried, they are pressable, and they sit behind the same toggle as the section marks.
rules.probe_notes: The probe that cut this passage died on a server overload after writing the rows and before writing its reasoning, so the website lane read the rows itself and records what they are. The passage is the postscript of Haktav Vehakabalah, and it is a discussion of the Masorah's own counting: rows 0 to 3 give a count of verses in words, row 8 names the Masorah, and rows 16 to 18 are the phrase for the half of the book by verses. So the note is text about the book rather than the book, which is exactly what rule 7 governs. Verified by reading the twenty rows, 2026-09-03, website lane.

rules.letter: W · a run, not a C0
rules.the_c0_law: No C0 of its own. The words are ordinary words; what is recorded is that a run of them is set apart.
rules.plainly: A commentary opens by quoting the words it is about, and the printers set that quotation apart. Stripping the setting apart as though it were transport loses a distinction the source drew, so it is recorded as an overlay over the run before anything is stripped: the ink stays what it was and the run says what it is.
rules.press: a word of the opening run

overlays.why: the printers set the opening quotation apart; in the source this project holds that is inline bold markup, which the builder refuses in ink. The reissue records it as an overlay instead, and this is that overlay: the ink is the body's own, with the markup removed and the run it marked recorded over it.

rules.probe_notes: Matnot Kehunah on Ruth Rabbah, one comment. Row 0 is an editorial siglum standing outside the quotation, so the overlay starts at row 1 and runs 5 rows: an offset the record has to carry, not a constant. The markup was removed from the ink and nothing else was changed.
